newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel asks Egypt's help finding Israeli.
newsitem.headline: Israel asks Egypt's help finding Israeli.

text.p: Israel said on Monday it had appealed to Egypt to help find an Israeli man abducted outside his Cairo area hotel.
"Israel appealed to the Egyptian government, and a meeting with the Egyptian interior minister is due to take place today," Israel's foreign ministry said in a statement.

Israel's charge d'affaires in Egypt, Jacob Gil, told Reuters Azam Azam, who had been working at a Cairo textile factory, was abducted while on his way back to the Baron Hotel in the suburb of Medinet Nasr last Wednesday.

"His father says people from security took him away. We checked this at a very high level and they know nothing about it. They have no reason not to tell us the truth," he said, adding he had asked to meet Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi.
Azam, in his late 30s, was chief mechanic at the factory.

An official at the Tefron company, the Israeli owner, said witnesses saw a group of about 10 well-dressed people, some with walkie-talkies, approach Azam at the entrance to the hotel as he got out of a cab. They asked a few questions and demanded to see his identification before taking him away.

Egypt's interior ministry said it had no information on the case. The Israeli foreign ministry said Foreign Minister David Levy would personally take up the case while in Cairo on Tuesday for a Middle East economic conference.
Egypt in 1979 became the first Arab state to sign a peace treaty with Israel.
